items.title: Flip Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: On the trumpets he had Roy Eldridge, Charlie Shavers, Dizzy Gillespie, Sweets, Fats Navarro, all the best in jazz.

ctx.x: Who else was on the tour? I know there was a lot of different people.

At the beginning, oh, at the very beginning we had everybody. He put together the best in jazz, the best in music, the best players. He was the only man that I know that could do a thing like that, to assemble a group like that. Well you had, your tenor saxophones was Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, Ben Webster, Illinois Jacquet, Stan Getz, Sonny Stitt — I hope I don’t leave anybody out — all the best. items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And that would go on for ….let’s see, Coleman Hawkins, Roy Eldridge, Flip Phillips, Bill Harris. After that, have an intermission and Ella Fitzgerald. I had quite a thrill on Jazz at the Philharmonic

ctx.x: Yes, we loved it. Because, there was no rehearsal. On the first night out, somebody would say in the dressing room, let’s play so and so and everybody would agree on it and then you go from there. And you play one fast tune, one medium tempo, then everybody would have a solo. Then you’d go to the piano player and tell him what key and what tune you wanted to play. And that would go on for ….let’s see, Coleman Hawkins, Roy Eldridge, Flip Phillips, Bill Harris. After that, have an intermission and Ella Fitzgerald.…

to Jimbo’s and play something.” I says, “Nooooooo, no. No, no, you remember this night, Jazz, I got to you tonight.” But it was just a ball to be on that Jazz at the Philharmonic. And then too, after that I got a band together in New York. I had Elvin Jones, Tommy Flanagan, Jimmy Forrest, and Joe Benjamin. I had a real good swinging band too, oh we were really doing it. I kept that band together for about six years.
